WHY_THE_NULL_RESULT_not_speculation: Disassembled both binaries with objdump: NEITHER contains a single vfmadd/vfmsub/vfnmadd/vfnmsub instruction (0 in each; 2224 and 1836 scalar mulsd respectively). clang here targets x86_64-w64-windows-gnu with no -march/-mtune anywhere in the 243-entry compile database, i.e. baseline x86-64, which predates FMA3. There was nothing to fuse, so turning fusion off changed nothing.
method: Two builds of the SAME source tree: the shared build/meson_test (242 TUs, 0 carrying -ffp-contract=off) and this bead's worktree build (243 TUs, 243/243 carrying it at effective -O2). Two independent game runs from each, dumped at --quant-decimals 15 (raw doubles), compared FULL PRECISION before any quantisation.

positive_control_the_flag_DOES_work.conclusion: The flag is load-bearing on an FMA-capable target and inert on this one. So the null result is a property of the TARGET, not of the flag or of the measurement.

quantisation_question_STILL_UNSETTLED: oo-ss8 could not locate a float noise floor because every value is an exact binary fraction needing at most 7 decimals, so toFixed(15) rounded nothing. This bead hoped two genuinely different builds would supply variation to measure. They did not: the two builds produce bit-identical output, so there is STILL no measured noise floor and 3 decimals remains a justified choice rather than a measured one. Nothing here narrows it. What would: an FMA-capable -march, a second platform, or a scenario that integrates motion.
what_this_means_for_the_policy: The -ffp-contract=off pin is INSURANCE, not a fix for this scenario on this host. It becomes load-bearing the moment anyone builds with -march=x86-64-v3 or newer, or on Phase 5's macos-arm64 (AArch64 has FMADD in its base ISA and clang contracts by default). Keeping it unconditionally is correct precisely because its absence is invisible here.
